newsitem.title: UK: UK's LSE no comment on talk of Heath probe.
newsitem.headline: UK's LSE no comment on talk of Heath probe.

text.p: The London stock exchange declined to comment on a newspaper report it was investigating activity in insurance broker C.E. Heath plc's shares ahead of an announcement of a possible management buyout made two weeks ago.
A spokeswoman for the exchange said it was policy not to comment on individual cases.
The report in the Mail on Sunday newspaper said that the exchange was understood to have examined the role played by stockbrokers in Ireland and Birmingham.
Heath announced after the close of trading on May 30 that senior management were in advanced talks about a possible buyout of the company for just under 100 million pounds.
That would value the shares at 143 pence each. The shares are currently trading at 130 pence.
Over three million shares changed hands, pushing the shares 14 pence higher in the course of business ahead of the late afternoon announcement.
According to sources close to the deal, it was the unusually high stock activity which prompted the company to release news of the talks.
Management involved in the possible offer include group chief executive John Mackenzie Green.
Non-executive directors were said by sources to be considering the approach but no further news has been released.
